alignments.note: οὕτως with a separate καί standing beside it: rule 100 gives the adverb the whole English correlative (here a bare *So*) and decides the particle on its own. Cf. JAS.1.11's *so … also*.
The correlative καί realized by *also* under rules 65 and 100; discontinuous from *So* under rule 15.
Noun stands bare, its determiner having gone to the article (rule 26).
Expressed copula; the predicate noun phrase spells itself out, so nothing is supplied here (rule 63 not in question).
Anarthrous attributive adjective takes a bare *little*; rule 58 puts the supplied determiner on the noun.
Rule 58: adjective and noun both anarthrous, so the supplied *a* belongs to the noun, discontinuously under rule 15.
Finite verb to *boasteth*. Variant SBLGNT.JAS.3.5.v005 is underdetermined and its base fallback is compatible with the ASV, so no textual decision arises here (rule 12).
Substantival adjective expanded with a generic English noun: rule 17 keeps the head on the adjective (*all things* heads on *All*).

Correlative adjective of degree rendered by a two-word English frame. Head on *much*, the dimension word carrying the lexeme's magnitude sense, with *how* its correlative helper under rule 7. Corrected from a head on *how*: rule 99 is scoped to the supplied *what manner of* frame over a QUALITY interrogative, where the following noun is an empty sortal completion (*what manner of persons*), and a dimension adjective is not that. Rule 91's operational test points the other way — `ἡλίκος` occurs nowhere in the corpus but inside this verse, and the neighbouring classes are unanimous: the sibling correlative `πηλίκος` → *how large* heads on *large* (GAL.6.11), `ὅσα` → *how much soever* on *much* (REV.18.7) and `ὅσαι` → *how many soever be* on *many* (2CO.1.20), and the `how …` frame heads its content word throughout. Rule 24's habit decides the rest: this chapter's own `τηλικοῦτος` → *so great* heads on *great* at JAS.3.4, and `τηλικοῦτος` heads on *great* in all three corpus units, so the demonstrative and interrogative members of one -λικος paradigm are analysed alike. (The ASV footnote *how great a forest* is an alternative rendering and is not aligned.)
Noun to *wood*; the ASV makes this the subject of its passive.
Active Greek verb rendered by an English passive; the auxiliary rides with the verb under rule 9 and rule 17 heads on the lexical participle *kindled*.

Greek nominative subject turned English agent phrase: the supplied *by* and the supplied determiner *a* both ride with the noun under rules 7 and 58, discontinuously under rule 15, and rule 17 heads on *fire*. The supplied *by* is licensed by the passive recast rather than by rule 21, which cannot reach it — a nominative has no case for a case preposition to realize, and this is the corpus's only nominative among the units whose English opens with *by*, the rest sitting on an expressed preposition or a dative. The one true precedent is 2CO.1.11, `εὐχαριστηθῇ` → *for thanks may be given*, where the Greek likewise makes the demoted argument nominative and the supplied word stays with the verb whose argument structure licenses it; that unit is `medium` and concedes the rule 21 reading, so it does not compel a placement. Giving *by* to `ἀνάπτει` on its model is therefore the competing reading, and marking it `added` under rule 5 a third; taken this way because the agent marker realizes this noun's own demoted role, and rule 11 keeps the ASV's markup from forcing `added`.

As with s014: head on *small*, the dimension word realizing the lexeme's magnitude sense, with *how* its correlative helper. Corrected from a head on *how* for the reasons given there — rule 99's frame is scoped to a quality interrogative with a supplied sortal noun, and rule 24 keeps this in step with JAS.3.4's `τηλικαῦτα` → *so great* headed on *great*. Variant SBLGNT.JAS.3.5.v006 is selected to the base and is not reopened here (rule 12).

review_notes: Reviewed and returned unchanged in structure: all sixteen units, their statuses, edges and heads stand as accepted. The only edit is an expansion of the s013 note to name the competing `added` reading for the supplied *by*, which rule 16 requires of a materially contested choice.

Partition verified: every s001–s016 and every t001–t023 appears exactly once, no ID invented, and every head is a member of its own array. All sixteen units are `aligned`, with no source-only or target-only unit in the verse.

οὕτως … καί is handled under rule 100: the adverb takes the whole English correlative (*So*), the separate particle takes the *also* the ASV writes, neither is joined to the other and neither is left empty. Rule 82 is not the case here, since οὕτως stands.

Both anarthrous adjective+noun pairs — μικρὸν μέλος and ἡλίκον πῦρ — follow rule 58: the supplied *a* goes to the noun, discontinuously under rule 15, and the adjective stays bare. Rule 51's supplied-determiner clause agrees, no Greek article standing in either phrase to compete.

The supplied agent marker *by* is kept as a rule 7 helper on πῦρ, the Greek nominative subject the ASV demotes in passivizing ἀνάπτει. It is not `added` under rule 86, whose test is whether a source token licenses the word: πῦρ does, being the phrase it marks. The alternative is now named in the unit note.

Both ἡλίκος units head on *how* under rule 99's operational reading, with the competing head on *much* and *small* named in each note. Rule 99's warning against decomposing the Greek — arguing that the lexeme's size element is what the dimension word glosses — is exactly the argument that would move these heads, and rule 91 replaces it with a query on the lemma. ἡλίκος is rare enough that a later chapter may find no corpus precedent; if one turns up heading a *how*-frame on the dimension word, these two units are where to revisit it.
The ASV's marginal *how great a forest* is an alternative rendering of ἡλίκην ὕλην and plays no part in the alignment; the text's *how much wood* is what is aligned.

Neither variant unit is reopened. SBLGNT.JAS.3.5.v005 is underdetermined over s009/s010 with r00-base among the readings the English permits, and SBLGNT.JAS.3.5.v006 is selected to base over s012; neither carries a FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE mark, so rule 97 is not in question and rule 12 forbids a fresh textual decision inside the alignment file.
